topic.title: Differentially Private Estimation and Selection
topic.overview: Differential privacy limits how much an algorithm’s output can reveal about an individual contribution. These papers study that requirement for estimation, hypothesis selection, streaming summaries, inference, and optimization. The central tradeoff involves statistical accuracy, computational cost, and the strength of protection under a specified notion of neighboring datasets.
topic.whyItMatters: A method can match an optimal error rate yet remain impractical because its computation is expensive or its constants are large. Private algorithms need guarantees that describe both useful output quality and realistic resource demands.
topic.evolution: Early representatives apply privacy to probabilistic inference and statistical estimators. Later work develops minimax analyses, privacy profiles, and amplification mechanisms. Recent examples accelerate private hypothesis selection and exploit structure in positive linear programs, while quantile and mean-estimation methods address heterogeneous data and shuffled access.
openQuestions: Which structural assumptions improve efficiency without weakening the intended privacy model?
How can practitioners compare mechanisms beyond a single reported privacy parameter pair?

papers.title: Mind the Gap: Mixtures of Gaussians in Approximate Differential Privacy
papers.tldr: Gaussian-mixture noise mechanisms reduce error for private scalar queries and approach optimality in the low-privacy regime.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Private Linear Regression via Iterative Hessian Mixing
papers.tldr: Iterative Hessian Mixing strengthens private least-squares error bounds and consistently outperforms evaluated baselines on bounded-data regression.

papers.title: Optimal conversion from Rényi Differential Privacy to $f$-Differential Privacy
papers.tldr: Intersecting single-order Rényi privacy regions yields the optimal black-box conversion from an RDP profile to a hypothesis-testing privacy trade-off.

papers.title: Persuasive Privacy
papers.tldr: A Bayesian game-theoretic framework unifies established privacy notions and supports purpose-driven guarantees, including for deterministic algorithms.

papers.title: Privacy-Aware Data Integration for Enhanced Quantile Inference under Heterogeneity
papers.tldr: Adaptive weighting combines quantile estimates across heterogeneous sites, with theoretical inference guarantees and support for local differential privacy.

papers.title: Shuffling-Aware Optimization for Private Vector Mean Estimation
papers.tldr: Optimizing private mean estimation specifically for shuffling yields an asymptotically optimal high-privacy mechanism with nearly central-Gaussian utility.

papers.title: Solving Positive Linear Programs with Differential Privacy
papers.tldr: New private solvers approximate positive linear programs while controlling constraint violations, with improved instance-dependent and new dimension-only guarantees.
